versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma is staged by subsite: supraglottis (epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds, arytenoids, false cords, ventricle), glottis (true cords, commissures) and subglottis. T reflects vocal-cord mobility (normal, impaired, fixed) and cartilage invasion: inner cortex of thyroid cartilage is T3, while invasion through the outer cortex or into extralaryngeal tissues is T4a; pre-epiglottic space invasion upstages supraglottic tumours. Nodal staging follows the head-and-neck ENE scheme; glottic cancers metastasise late because the cords are lymphatic-poor.

t.label: Tumour limited to one subsite with normal vocal-cord mobility (glottis: limited to cord(s) with normal mobility; T1a one cord, T1b both cords)
Tumour invades more than one adjacent subsite (e.g. supraglottis plus glottis) or has impaired vocal-cord mobility, without fixation
Tumour limited to larynx with vocal-cord fixation, and/or invasion of postcricoid area, pre-epiglottic space, paraglottic space, and/or inner cortex of thyroid cartilage
Moderately advanced disease: invasion through outer cortex of thyroid cartilage and/or into extralaryngeal tissues (trachea, strap muscles, thyroid gland, oesophagus)
Very advanced disease: invasion of prevertebral space, encasement of carotid artery, or invasion of mediastinal structures

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Single ipsilateral node 3 cm or smaller, extranodal extension negative (ENE-)
Single ipsilateral node larger than 3 cm up to 6 cm, ENE-
Multiple ipsilateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Bilateral or contralateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Any node larger than 6 cm, ENE-
Any node with clinically overt extranodal extension (ENE+)

versions.regionalNodes: Levels II, III and IV (jugular chain) and VI (prelaryngeal/Delphian, pretracheal, paratracheal); supraglottic tumours also drain to levels I and V. Bilateral or contralateral nodes upstage to N2c.
versions.histologicGrade: Well differentiated (G1), moderately differentiated (G2), poorly differentiated (G3); transglottic spread and cartilage invasion are reported independently of grade.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Conventional squamous cell carcinoma; verrucous carcinoma (rare, pushing front); basaloid, papillary and spindle-cell (sarcomatoid) variants; neuroendocrine carcinoma and minor salivary tumours of the larynx are staged by their own systems.
prognosticFactors: Vocal-cord mobility (normal vs impaired vs fixed)
Cartilage invasion (inner vs through outer cortex)
Subsite (glottic tumours present early, supraglottic spread silently)
